# Quality Manual Extract (Synthetic Fixture)

This file is a synthetic, hand-written fixture for plan 06.1-07's retrieval
evaluation harness. It is not real regulated content and does not copy any
external standard's text -- see the plan's own threat register (T-06.1-37).

## Document Control

Controlled documents at this site are governed by the document control
procedure QMS-DC-001. Every controlled document carries a unique document
number, a current effective revision, and an approval record signed by the
process owner and the quality unit before release. A document reaches
effective status only after both electronic signatures are captured in the
document management system. Superseded revisions are archived, never
deleted, and remain retrievable for the full retention period defined in
the site retention schedule. Document EVAL-DOC-204 is the reference example
used throughout this manual extract for illustrating the controlled-document
life cycle from draft through periodic review. Uncontrolled copies,
including printed extracts, must be marked "For Reference Only" and are not
valid for use in GxP operations. Any employee who identifies an uncontrolled
or expired document in active use must report it through the quality event
system so the document owner can correct the distribution.

## Change Control

Proposed changes to a qualified system, process, or controlled document are
raised as a change request and evaluated by the change control board before
implementation. The board assesses regulatory impact, validation impact,
and training impact for every submitted request, and assigns a risk
classification of low, medium, or high before approval. A high-risk change
requires a full impact assessment covering every linked system, control,
and procedure, plus a post-implementation effectiveness check performed no
sooner than thirty days after go-live. Change request CR-EVAL-058
illustrates a medium-risk classification: a labeling template update that
required revalidation of the associated print verification test but did not
require revalidation of the underlying software. No change is implemented
in a production GxP system without a closed, approved change record
referencing the specific systems and documents affected.

## Training Records

Personnel performing GxP-relevant tasks must complete role-based training
before independently performing those tasks, and training completion is
recorded in the learning management system against the specific document
revision trained on. When a controlled document is revised, every role
mapped to that document receives a retraining assignment automatically, and
the prior revision's training record remains linked for audit trace-back.
Training record TRN-EVAL-091 demonstrates the expected linkage: employee,
document number, document revision, training date, and assessment result
recorded together as one auditable unit. A gap between a document's
effective date and an assigned employee's retraining completion date is
tracked as an open training gap and reported at the monthly quality review
until closed.

## Periodic Review

Every controlled document and qualified system is subject to periodic
review on a fixed interval defined by its criticality classification,
typically annually for high-criticality systems and biennially for
lower-criticality systems. The periodic review confirms the document or
system still reflects current practice, current regulatory expectations,
and current validated state, and results in either a reaffirmation, a
revision, or a retirement decision. Periodic review record PR-EVAL-033 is
an example of a reaffirmation outcome: the review team confirmed no changes
were needed and extended the review due date by the standard interval. A
periodic review that is overdue by more than thirty days is escalated to
the quality unit as a compliance finding requiring a documented corrective
action.
